method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text with the writing-l4-rules skill (and references/regulative.md), from the seat of the claimant in a Queensland personal injury claim, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18 and the rulings on negatives of 2026-11-04 and 2026-11-05; dates in one module, the rules and the claimant's exported questions in another (each question calls a rule defined beside it), worked cases in a third; six regulative rules run by EVALTRACE inside exported questions that take only plain facts; no REFUSE; checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.

scope: The claims procedure of chapter 2 as the claimant meets it. In: s 6 (application); ss 9, 9A (notice of claim and initial notice: to whom, by when, if late), 10(1) and 13 (as they fix the part 2 day), 18, 19; division 1A, ss 20B-20J (child injured by medical treatment); s 20(1), (4); ss 22(5), (6), (8), 24, 25, 27(2), 29A(5) with 32 and 35; ss 36(2), (3), 37(1), 39(1), 40(4), (9), 42; ss 43, 44; ss 48(1), 56 (with 6(4), 43(5)), 59. Out: division 1AA and ss 9B, 9C, 13A, 61 (law practice certificates); respondent and contributor procedure (ss 10(2)-(5), 11, 12, 14-17, 28-31, 33, 34, 41); conference conduct and offer form (ss 37(2)-(5), 38, 40(1)-(3), (5)-(8)); ss 47, 48(2), 57, 60; chapter 3 (advertising, touting, claim referrals, s 71E); chapter 4 (transitional); machinery. Periods left to the regulation take the Act's fallback; the s 75A offer and costs limits are asked. Reasons in NOTES.md.
